Zboriv Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Ternopilska oblast, Ukraine

Demolished. In the early 18th century, 15 Zboriv Jews were falsely accused of murdering a Christian beggar and later exonerated; the community subsequently celebrated an annual local holiday, 'Purim Katan,' on Shvat 12 to commemorate their deliverance. In the late 18th century, Moshe Shapiro, a student of Dov Ber of Mezeritch — successor to the Baal Shem Tov, documented elsewhere in this collection — lived in Zboriv, and a Hasidic court founded by Meir Moskovich was seated in the town from 1867 to 1914. This cemetery is marked on a map in the 1975 Yizkor memorial book Sefer Zikaron li-kehilat Zborov. On July 4, 1941, the day of the German occupation, more than 1,000 Jews were executed; only 25 of Zboriv's Jews survived the war.
